competitors.title: Securing AI Agents Before They Go Rogue Is Next to Impossible
key_points: Gartner's Dennis Xu: 90% of agentic AI offerings are low-autonomy, 10% are high-autonomy with broad tool/data access
Jailbreaks are the #1 reason AI agents are risky — LLMs will always be susceptible
PocketOS incident: AI coding agent deleted production database and volume-level backups in 9 seconds
Four-step security program: agent discovery, AI security posture management, pen testing/red teaming, strong agent defenses
84% of AI agents can access sensitive data; 67% believe agents already accessed data they shouldn't have
Behavior-based detection at runtime is needed but 'there's no easy way to do that' — emerging area with unproven solutions
Permission right-sizing and tooling right-sizing concepts from traditional security apply to agents

competitors.title: Agentic AI Isn't Risky; the Way Orgs Deploy It Is
key_points: Acronis research: agentic vulnerabilities are mostly a byproduct of traditionally bad coding, not AI itself
AI agent = deterministic system (tools/software) + non-deterministic system (LLM) — vulnerabilities arise at the intersection
Old world vulnerabilities in agentic AI: lack of input sanitization, hardcoded credentials, insufficient access controls
Salesforce critical vulnerability: malicious prompt in form led AI agent to carry out instructions
ServiceNow exploit chain: overly permissive chatbot with factory default credential allowed creating powerful AI agents
Need 'old world principles with a new world spin' — token-based authentication, access controls applied to AI
